title: Design an API Spec and Database Schema
description: Create an OpenAPI specification and ERD for a student management system using Swagger Editor and dbdiagram.io
objective: Students will create a valid OpenAPI 3.0 specification in Swagger Editor and design a database schema with an ERD using dbdiagram.io

steps.title: Set Up Your API Spec File
steps.instructions:
Open your `attendance-tracker-spec` folder (from Lab 16-A).

Create a new file called `api-spec.yaml`.

Start with the OpenAPI boilerplate:

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: SmartAttend API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Student attendance management API for TechPath Institute

servers:
  - url: http://localhost:8000/api/v1
    description: Local development

paths: {}

components:
  schemas: {}
```

Now open **Swagger Editor** in your browser: https://editor.swagger.io

Clear the default content and paste your YAML. Verify it shows "No errors" at the top.

If you see errors, check your indentation — YAML uses spaces (2 spaces per level), not tabs.

steps.title: Define Reusable Schemas
steps.instructions:
Replace the empty `components.schemas` with your data models:

```yaml
components:
  securitySchemes:
    BearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: JWT

  schemas:
    Student:
      type: object
      required: [name, email]
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
          example: 1
        name:
          type: string
          example: "Rahul Sharma"
        email:
          type: string
          format: email
          example: "rahul@techpath.biz"
        phone:
          type: string
          example: "9876543210"
        batch:
          type: string
          example: "PFS-2026-July"
        city:
          type: string
          example: "Bhopal"
        is_active:
          type: boolean
          default: true

    Attendance:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
        student_id:
          type: integer
        date:
          type: string
          format: date
          example: "2026-07-25"
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [present, absent, late]
          example: "present"
        marked_by:
          type: string
          example: "Amit Kumar"
```

Add one more schema called `AttendanceReport` with fields: `student_name`, `total_classes`, `present_count`, `absent_count`, `percentage`.

Paste the updated YAML into Swagger Editor and verify there are no errors.

steps.title: Add API Endpoints
steps.instructions:
Replace the empty `paths: {}` with real endpoints. Add at least these 6:

```yaml
paths:
  /auth/login:
    post:
      summary: Login with email and password
      tags: [Auth]
      security: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [email, password]
              properties:
                email:
                  type: string
                  example: "rahul@techpath.biz"
                password:
                  type: string
                  example: "mypassword123"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Login successful
        "401":
          description: Invalid credentials

  /students:
    get:
      summary: List all students
      tags: [Students]
      parameters:
        - name: batch
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: skip
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 0
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 20
      responses:
        "200":
          description: List of students
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  success:
                    type: boolean
                  data:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      $ref: "#/components/schemas/Student"

    post:
      summary: Create a new student
      tags: [Students]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/Student"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Student created
        "409":
          description: Email already exists

  /students/{student_id}:
    get:
      summary: Get student by ID
      tags: [Students]
      parameters:
        - name: student_id
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: integer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Student details
        "404":
          description: Student not found

  /attendance:
    post:
      summary: Mark attendance
      tags: [Attendance]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/Attendance"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Attendance recorded

  /reports/attendance:
    get:
      summary: Get attendance report
      tags: [Reports]
      parameters:
        - name: batch
          in: query
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Attendance report
```

Add 2 more endpoints of your own choosing (for example: update student, delete student, get attendance by student ID, or bulk mark attendance).

Paste into Swagger Editor and verify all endpoints appear in the UI.

steps.title: Design the Database Schema with ERD
steps.instructions:
Open **dbdiagram.io** in your browser: https://dbdiagram.io

Clear the default content and write your schema using DBML (Database Markup Language):

```dbml
Table students {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  name varchar(100) [not null]
  email varchar(200) [unique, not null]
  phone varchar(15)
  batch_id integer [ref: > batches.id]
  city varchar(50)
  is_active boolean [default: true]
  created_at timestamp [default: `now()`]
  updated_at timestamp
}

Table batches {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  name varchar(100) [not null]
  trainer_id integer [ref: > trainers.id]
  start_date date
  end_date date
  city varchar(50)
  created_at timestamp [default: `now()`]
}

Table trainers {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  name varchar(100) [not null]
  email varchar(200) [unique, not null]
  phone varchar(15)
  is_active boolean [default: true]
  created_at timestamp [default: `now()`]
}

Table attendances {
  id integer [pk, increment]
  student_id integer [ref: > students.id, not null]
  date date [not null]
  status varchar(10) [not null, note: 'present, absent, or late']
  marked_by integer [ref: > trainers.id]
  created_at timestamp [default: `now()`]
}
```

After pasting, you should see a visual ERD with lines connecting the tables.

Add one more table of your own (for example: `subjects`, `announcements`, or `feedback`).

Export the diagram as a PNG image. Save it as `erd.png` in your project folder.

steps.title: Write SQLAlchemy Models and Seed Data
steps.instructions:
Create a file called `models.py` in your project folder.

Translate your ERD into SQLAlchemy 2.0 models:

```python
# models.py — SQLAlchemy models for SmartAttend

from datetime import datetime
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Boolean, Date, DateTime, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, DeclarativeBase


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Trainer(Base):
    __tablename__ = "trainers"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String(100), nullable=False)
    email = Column(String(200), unique=True, nullable=False)
    phone = Column(String(15))
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    batches = relationship("Batch", back_populates="trainer")


class Batch(Base):
    __tablename__ = "batches"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String(100), nullable=False)
    trainer_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("trainers.id"))
    start_date = Column(Date)
    end_date = Column(Date)
    city = Column(String(50))
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    trainer = relationship("Trainer", back_populates="batches")
    students = relationship("Student", back_populates="batch")


class Student(Base):
    __tablename__ = "students"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String(100), nullable=False)
    email = Column(String(200), unique=True, nullable=False)
    phone = Column(String(15))
    batch_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("batches.id"))
    city = Column(String(50))
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    batch = relationship("Batch", back_populates="students")
    attendances = relationship("Attendance", back_populates="student")


class Attendance(Base):
    __tablename__ = "attendances"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    student_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("students.id"), nullable=False)
    date = Column(Date, nullable=False)
    status = Column(String(10), nullable=False)  # present, absent, late
    marked_by = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("trainers.id"))
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    student = relationship("Student", back_populates="attendances")
```

Verify your Python files have no syntax errors by running:
```bash
python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('models.py').read()); print('models.py OK')"
python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('seed_data.py').read()); print('seed_data OK')"
```

You now have a complete Spec-Kit: PRD, API spec, ERD, models, and seed data — all created before writing a single line of application code.
